legend.summary: The globe turns slowly from Asia across Africa to the Americas while seven weeks of early 2020 go by. A fixed scan line runs down the middle of the Earth, pole to pole, and reads the carbon dioxide that passes under it.
legend.method: Everything you hear sits on the scan line. Stereo runs along the line: the north (top of the globe) sounds in your left ear, the south (bottom) in your right. Latitude is also pitch: 17 bands of 9°, the farther north, the higher the note.

items.meaning: All the carbon dioxide on the line. It grows louder and brighter as carbon dioxide builds, and turns tense and slightly dissonant over the densest plumes. It is quiet over clean ocean air.
Dense plumes from fires, cities and industry, played as their thickest part crosses the line. Louder = denser; the very densest ring in a darker, minor colour.
One double beat for each day of data, at midnight UTC. Carbon dioxide over land really does pulse daily, as fires and plants follow the Sun.

legend.caveat: NASA's colour key for this visualization has no numbers, so levels are relative: faint tan is the least carbon dioxide shown, orange is more, red is the most. Values are read from the colours of the video frames, not from the model output.
